C0839.title: Weak Government Email Password Leads to Theft of 2,000 Classified Documents
C0839.summary: In November 2025, several media outlets, citing Baomiguan and related public material, reported a weak-password espionage case: a municipal bureau used overly simple credentials for a work email account, with the password reportedly set to the office telephone number. A foreign intelligence service guessed the credentials and stole nearly 2,000 documents, including sensitive information such as local troop deployments. The case shows that weak passwords on government or key-position accounts can let attackers enter email systems at low cost and steal sensitive material at scale.
